## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A two-fascicle compendium of *karmavācanā* drawn from the *Sìfēn lǜ* ([KR6k0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0009)) by **Dàoxuān** 道宣 ([道宣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%AE%A3)), founder of the **Nánshān** 南山 *Vinaya* school. 刪補 *shānbǔ* "pruned and supplemented" indicates the editorial method: Dàoxuān selected, ordered, and where necessary supplemented the *karmavācanā* formulae of the parent Vinaya for practical use. 隨機 *suíjī* "adapting to circumstances" emphasises the practical-pastoral orientation. Composed at Zhōngnánshān 終南山 between 635 and 660 CE, the text became the **single most widely used *karmavācanā* compendium** in East Asian Buddhism.

**Abstract**

The *Sìfēn lǜ shānbǔ suíjī jiémó* is one of the **three foundational works** of Dàoxuān's Nánshān school — together with the *Sìfēn lǜ shānfán bǔquē xíngshì chāo* ([KR6k0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0128)) and the *Sìfēn lǜ bǐqiū hánzhù jièběn* ([KR6k0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0131)). Together these are known as the *Three Great Works of the Nánshān school* (南山三大部 *Nánshān sān dàbù*). After the imperial canonisation of the *Sìfēn lǜ* in 709 CE, Dàoxuān's compilations became the universal practical Vinaya manuals of East Asian Buddhism. The present text on *karmavācanā* — the procedural formulae for monastic legal acts — supplied the practical handbook for every Chinese, Korean, Japanese, and Vietnamese monastery's conduct of *upasaṃpadā*, *uposatha*, *pravāraṇā*, *kaṭhina*, *vassa*, and the various *adhikaraṇa* procedures.

The text was further commented on and reorganised in subsequent generations: **Yuánzhào** 元照 ([元照](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E7%85%A7)) of the Sòng wrote the *Sìfēnlǜ shānbǔ suíjī jiémó shū* (X40n728); **Huáisù** ([懷素](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%87%B7%E7%B4%A0)) of the early Tang produced his own competing recension as the *Sēng jiémó* ([KR6k0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0047)); these later works supplement but did not displace Dàoxuān's foundational compilation.
